title: LG 635 Litre Side by Side Instaview Fridge GS-V600MBLC $1787 + Delivery @ Harvey Norman
body:
Deal: LG 635 Litre Side by Side Instaview Fridge GS-V600MBLC $1787 + Delivery @ Harvey Norman

[4rd] I currently have a side by side and they are clumsy to get wider items into (trays/pans/etc, need to angle them in if you can and spillage etc), even worse if fridge is near a corner or adjacent wall as door will not open fully. French door allows both doors to be opened and better overall access. Still a good buy if access is not an issue, however worth considering just in case as I regret my SxS purchase and will ensure next buy is a french door version.
[mshanann] How modern is your SxS though? The freezer component of this LG fridge can directly accept an item flat at up to 31cm wide, whilst the fridge component can accept an item up to 45cm wide without any angling. I agree on the access requirement though - the doors of this LG side-by-side open to about 45 degrees. \_/
As someone tall, I much prefer the side-by-side and being able to clearly see what is present in my freezer.
[dangerdanger] Agree. Go for French door, with freezer at the bottom.
I recently bought the 847L version - doors open wide and I have the full width of the fridge to store things
[mshanann] The LG 847l french door fridge is nearly $5000 - this is sub $1800
[dangerdanger] Yep, with limitations. Smaller volume, SxS (not french door). But worth compromising for price
As per 4rd above, perhaps SxS is for you
[d2567] Great price . Purchased mine in January. Was on sale then for about $1900 instead of up to $3500.
Spherical ice cubes are a summer bonus.
Access through window for milk and drinks is something we didn't think we needed but use around a dozen times a day.
[justtoreply] I'd be embarrassed to have a fridge with a window.
[ShanoDD] These cost an ARM and a leg but worth it.
[soupratt] Avoid LG unless you have no choice. Had a similar LG fridge for 6 years and it failed 4 times during that period of time not including other smaller things which I replaced like the ice maker. The door wiring is fragile and they fail after a few years requiring a whole new door. Fortunately, the first one was covered under warranty but the other 2 times it wasn't and despite paying for a replacement myself, it failed again within 12 months. The repair person (not LG but a LG assigned repairer) said it is a common failing point, as well as the flimsy plastics and ice maker.
The trouble is that when any of the doors fail, the ice maker will not work and the door open alarm will keep sounding (you can turn it off). When the door with the digital controls fail you can't adjust the fridge.
LG support are next to useless and basically tell you go Go F yourself when just out of warranty. They don't even care their replacement parts fail in less than 12 months.
The LGs are ok to look and if you need to get one, make sure you get the longest extended warranty you can get. You will need it.
[Ijuiceman] Mate, I have a LG French Door fridge with Plumbed water/ice and its been 17 years and still going strong. Far better than Samsung that I was looking at the sme time. My mate had a LG and 3 years into the use the ice maker died. They could not get the parts for it, so they gave him a new fridge. LG were a little slow initially, but came through in the end.
[soupratt] 17 years ago they might have been fine but the current crop aren't great. And yeah, Samsung are even worse.
[fish93] Agree LG is terrible. We had an LG French door for 4.5 years and the compressor broke. Luckily just within the 5 year warranty period. Castle LG and they sent someone out to fix it. Not even a month later, something else broke. This time, as we were away from home, everything in the fridge and freezer went off as we came home to a fridge that had been broken for days.
At this point, we didn’t need more trouble with the fridge. LG ended up giving us a refund and we bought a Mitsubishi French door.
[HDay] Amazimg to know how good their service is. Refund 🥰. 5 years of free use.
[mshanann] This lg has a different compressor design though I imagine. LG recently updated its refrigerator compressor design—moving away from the problematic linear inverter style toward more robust reciprocal/smart inverter designs
[4mOzfan] I also had a very good experience with my LG washing machine. LG replaced its faulty water level sensor recently (bought 2021) citing they offer 10 years warranty on motor.
This has made me think if I should buy a LG dishwasher as well!
[Not Applicable] I thought the thumbnail was one of those Dell office PCs haha
[tsugnev] I have this fridge. I also love this fridge, particularly the ice balls lol.
[Bugishere] Similar price on LG education portal and can stack with 10/15% off 2000/4000 spend or $50 welcome coupon.
[BiggieSmalls] Great fridge. Have had this model since January (paid $1,888 back then via appliances central). No complaints at all.
[talentmyj] If you ever deal with LG customer service here. You will never buy LG products
[bleeder] Can I hijack this post? Moving in to a new house in about a month, need a new fridge, have no idea what to look for. Any tips?
[GreenLego] I love my 7 star energy rating fridge. I was surprised by how bad my old fridge was in terms of electricity use. The 7 star fridge has used 99kwh for the first 7 months of this year.
[Jarr0d] Wow only 99kwh? How many litres?
I have this fridge and tested it with my anker 2kwh powerstation, i get just over 24hours from it. So i would guess around 700kwh year
[GreenLego] 417L
It looks like 7 star fridges aren't popular anymore and manufacturers have moved onto 8 star fridges now.
My previous one that was more than 20 years old was using crazy amount of electricity, like 130kwh in a single month. I think it was like 2.5 stars or something. I never realised how efficient fridges has gotten.
[bleeder] Good tip, I'll check energy efficiency closely when shopping
